summary: The exchange request now converts a fetch rejection into PassportError(502), so network failures and AbortSignal timeouts return 502 passport_unavailable and the outer catch clears the state and verifier cookies, while 4xx exchange responses still return 401 invalid_api_key. A new Bun callback-route test covers fetch rejection, timeout rejection and the invalid-token 401 case.

evidence: src/auth/passport.ts:316-318 turns an exchange fetch rejection into PassportError(502); errorResponse maps 502 to passport_unavailable.
src/auth/passport.ts:329-333 appends clearStateCookie and clearVerifierCookie to the error response, clearing the state cookie on the 502 path.
src/auth/passport.ts:319-322 leaves the 4xx exchange branch on PassportError() so invalid credentials still return 401 invalid_api_key.

tests/passport-exchange.test.ts:42-72 drives handlePassportRoute for /auth/login then /auth/callback with TypeError, DOMException TimeoutError and invalid-token fixtures, asserting 502 passport_unavailable and 401 invalid_api_key with cleared transient cookies.
